summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 2.31/5057)

data.turoyo: Aloho frəḏle ʕal u ʕəlmo, mərle: "Šġalu w axulu!" <...>
data.translation: God imposed it upon the world, saying: "Work and eat!" <...>

rationale: First Preterit box and sense 2: overt prescribing agent, ʕal-obligatee and quoted content. English is the supplied project machine translation, quoted unchanged, not an edition translation.

Aloho is agent of frəḏle, ʕal u ʕəlmo marks the obligated group, and the work-and-eat quotation supplies the prescribed content. This differs in valency and meaning from a theme belonging by right to an l-entitled person in 1. One attestation; preserve plain ḏ in the source.

data.turoyo: Madamki hawxa yo, i aṯto kofərḏ̣o lu gawro qamoyo.
data.translation: Wenn das so ist, so gehört die Frau von Rechtswegen dem ersten Mann.

rationale: Better standalone context for a thin cell: explicit female subject and l-marked entitled person. 60/127 is already a parallel reference, but this ruling’s actual text is not quoted.

summary: All five occurrences support I.1 von Rechtswegen gehören. The female subject controls -o; l- marks the legally entitled person, including eli, elux and lu gawro qamoyo. These are not transitive imposed-duty constructions merely because the Arabic etymology includes that meaning.

The first two verses each contain two alternative predicates, and 60/127 states the ruling. Count five occurrence decisions, not five independent examples. One additional full ruling is enough; retain all inherited references and wording.
g-, gəd-, k- and ko- occur with the same Infectum predicate. They do not license a ko-Preterit box, since there is no Preterit base with an agent-series suffix here.

Read both round-1 files and the sole Jan occurrence. Round 1 established only legal entitlement with l- and female themes. Jan supplies an independently attested agentive Preterit with ʕal-obligatee; the Arabic etymology alone would not justify it.
No Detransitive or stem change is involved. Quoted content is the imposed instruction; no unexpressed nominal direct object is invented. New Preterit box does not duplicate the old Infectum examples.

Jan 2.31/5057: is plain ḏ in frəḏle the author’s regular notation for the root’s emphatic consonant, or a local spelling? Source text is preserved. Confirm other subjects/content types for new sense 2.
